question: A teammate writes `@Autowired private CourseRepository repository;` in a service and then wants a unit test with a fake repository and no Spring. What is the problem?
options: The field cannot be set without reflection or a running container, because there is no constructor parameter to pass the fake to
Spring forbids tests that do not start the container
A fake repository can never implement the interface
The annotation makes the field static
explanation: With constructor injection the test calls new CourseService(fake). A private injected field has no such entry point, so the test needs reflection or the container.

question: The application class is `com.example.courseapi.CourseApiApplication`. A new `@Service` is created in `com.example.billing`. The app fails at startup because a controller needs it. What is the most likely cause?
options: @Service only works in packages named service
The billing package is outside the scanned package tree, so the service is never registered as a bean
Spring Boot allows only one @Service per application
The service needs the @Primary annotation
explanation: Component scanning covers the package of the application class and its sub-packages. com.example.billing is a sibling of com.example.courseapi, so the class is skipped.

question: Two beans implement `Notifier`, and a service asks for a single `Notifier` parameter. Startup fails. Which change fixes it while keeping both beans?
options: Rename the parameter to notifier2
Make both beans prototype scoped
Mark one bean with @Primary, or add @Qualifier with a bean name to the parameter
Delete the interface and inject the concrete classes by field
explanation: Injection by type is ambiguous when two beans match. @Primary sets a default and @Qualifier names the wanted bean, so both implementations can stay.

question: A singleton `ReportService` has a constructor parameter of a prototype-scoped `ReportBuilder`. Every report ends up appending to the same builder. Why?
options: Prototype beans are always shared
The builder is injected once when the singleton is created, so the singleton keeps that one instance
Spring creates a new service for every call
@Scope is ignored on classes that have a constructor
explanation: Injection happens once, at construction. Injecting an ObjectProvider<ReportBuilder> and calling getObject() on each use returns a fresh prototype every time.

question: A singleton controller stores the current user's name in a field during each request so that helper methods can read it. What goes wrong under concurrent requests?
options: Nothing, each request gets its own controller
The container throws an exception on the second request
The field becomes final
Requests overwrite each other's value, because one singleton instance serves all threads
explanation: The default scope is singleton, so one instance handles all requests. Per-request data belongs in method parameters or a request-scoped bean, never in a singleton field.
